facts.fact: Bridge Fiber Solutions' director general says the state-built national backbone of about 3,000 km, with 61 points of presence on part of the network, has been commercially operated since March 2023 and covers practically the whole territory.
Bridge Fiber Solutions' director general says a new 43 km Ouarkoye-Mana segment was built in 2026, with new points of presence at Mogtedo, Pa, Houndé and Mana.

Bridge Fiber Solutions says it sells capacity, dark fibre and wavelengths on the state backbone to 44 customers in 2026 (7 in 2023), including all three mobile operators, ISPs, state firms and banks, on a price catalogue validated annually by ARCEP and the ministry, with non-discrimination.

facts.fact: The document records the SMART Burkina project, financed by a Chinese concessional loan from China Eximbank (about 47 billion CFA francs) and implemented by Huawei and CITCC, as starting in 2020 to build about 800 km of fibre linking 22 major Burkinabe cities.
The document states the SMART Burkina project, about 800 km of fibre connecting 22 major cities across Burkina Faso, was completed in August 2025, citing a SASAC report.

systems.platform: fibre optic, built by Huawei and CITCC

facts.fact: The document states that on 29 September 2020 China Eximbank and Burkina Faso's Ministry of Security signed an RMB 560 million loan to finance a commercial contract with Huawei and CITCC for a 650 km fibre optic backbone linking cities and localities, plus a 150 km fibre network.
The document states the project officially commenced on 8 July 2021, with completion expected within 54 months (8 January 2026).

facts.fact: The document states construction of Phase 1 of the National Telecommunications Backbone Project (PBNT), a 307 km fibre link from Ouagadougou to Po under a contract with Huawei, began on 10 December 2017.

The document states PBNT Phase 1, a 307 km fibre backbone linking Ouagadougou and Po (capacity 1,600 Gbit/s, serving ten municipalities), was completed and officially inaugurated on 26 October 2021; it is part of a planned 5,740 km, EUR 175 million programme.
Minister Aminata Zerbo/Sabane told parliament the national backbone now offers robust connectivity across the whole territory.
